subject: Transportation Systems
title: The World Speed Record
description: Learn The World Speed Record in one minute.

hook.text: In 2007, a French TGV test train hit 357 mph. The rails glowed orange behind it.

buildup.text: The run used shortened cars, extra power, and specially prepared track. It wasn't a normal service.

discovery.text: That record still stands for conventional wheeled rail. Only maglev trains have gone faster.

twist.text: Commercial TGV trains run at 200 mph max. The gap between record and reality is enormous.

climax.text: Records push engineering limits but daily service needs reliability, not raw speed.

punchline.text: The fastest train ever ran once. The useful ones run daily.

quiz.question: What speed did the French TGV reach in its 2007 test run?
